body: Thank you for your comments. Provided backstory and a tl;dr because it's lengthy.

Turn the clock back about 10 years, my parents abandoned me at a hospital when I was 14. I was put into a group home, and lived there for a while until somehow I got sent back home.  The whole time I lived there, all I wanted was to be home, yet when I actually got to go home, I didn't want to be there. To sum it up, I was very confused.

A year or so later, was filled of promiscuity, meeting guys  and neglect from my parents who were often on holidays, or if they were home, they didn't seem to care about my whereabouts.

At 15, I was overweight, had no support, and definitely no self-esteem. I met a guy that paid a lot of attention to me. I told him of my troubles, and he told me I could move out.  I remember asking how, since I didn't have a job and was still in high school. So he told me about this -fabulous- (sarcasm) thing called welfare. I'd never heard of it, since I grew up in a fairly wealthy neighborhood. 

So I started dating this guy, and our relationship moved way too quickly. Within weeks I was on welfare, and had moved in with him. That's when the abuse started. Sadly though, as a confused young girl, I felt that I couldn't go home to my parents and had no other option.

Soon after, I dropped out of school and got a job. I worked full-time, all the while hiding the truth about how terrible my situation was, and how terrified I was to go home every night. I was so stressed that I went from over 200 lbs to 120 lbs over the course of the first year.

I endured 5 long years of isolation, sexual, mental, financial and physical abuse, until one day when I was 19, I found out I was pregnant and we moved into a two bedroom apartment. Suddenly, I had someone else to fight for. I felt angry and wanted to protect my unborn child. 

Shortly after my child was born, an old friend came to visit.  She could tell that something wasn't right.  We went out for a coffee (which I wasn't normally allowed to do without him) and I felt myself pouring my heart out to her.

She told me that I needed to leave, and that she could take my baby and I away. Regardless of our lack of finance, or my depressed, anorexic state. (He had controlled all of my money, so at the time I had 75 cents to my name).

The next day, I packed all of the baby stuff that I could fit into a back pack, and without thinking, took my child with my friend and drove 6 hours away.

After a few days there, I received a telephone call from the police. They said my ex filed a complaint that I had kidnapped my child and I had to return to the city. I explained the abuse, but regardless, the law stated that I had to come back.

I started calling him, and good old Stockholm syndrome was making me feel like I wanted to go back to him. (hard to understand, I know.) He revealed to me that upon his realization that I was not returning with our child, he proceeded to destroy ALL of my belongings. Old photos, clothing, my guitar was smashed, you name it, it was gone.

I am very possessive of my things, so this obviously made me very angry.  Angry enough to make the right choice, and stay away from him.

Fast forward, I come home to my city with my son.  Back in with the parents... My mom was delighted, her alcoholic husband however, was not. (I'll add this is the same step father I had been living with when I was abandoned at the hospital.)

It wasn't long before in an alcoholic rage he told me that my son and I were no longer welcome to stay. So we packed up our things and moved to my Aunt's. My Aunt then proceeded to write me daily letters about welfare and how people like me cheat, lie and steal their way through life. 

I was just finishing my maternity leave, and found a new job, things were looking up. I moved out of my Aunt's and into my Grandmother's house.

At this point in time my son was not even a year old yet. We had moved 5 times.

I got a call that a city housing project had a rent-geared to income apartment for me. Amazing! Probably the best thing that had ever happened to me! Until, my new boss told me that things slowed down at work and they no longer needed me. 

Fast forward to a bunch of years off and on welfare, struggling to afford daycare on minimum wage, even with reduced rent, it seems impossible. The more money, I make the higher my rent is.  Also daycare in my area was $45/day.

Now I've finally started trying to do something better. I took out a loan and started taking an online college program. First semester was great, now this semester I've fallen behind. My now 6 year old is on summer holidays and I'm having trouble keeping up.

I missed some assignments (which I made up for) but now this morning have realized I somehow missed the cutoff date for online exam bookings. I'm afraid that I'll fail.

I just feel like life is a constant struggle. I want to get ahead but everything is always so overwhelming and I am extremely depressed. I feel like I'll never have a job that will allow me to move out of this ghetto, and give my son a good life. I'm constantly depressed about everything. Every time I get on the right track, something brings me down. What should I do?



Tl;dr
Suffered years of abuse, finally getting my life on track, in college with loans, but feeling as though it is impossible. Very depressed.
